import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.27

by H. Koch

Prove that a torsion-free pro-$p$ group with one defining relation has
$p$-cohomological dimension $2$.

Here one defining relation has its standard pro-$p$ meaning: the group is
topologically finitely generated and its relation rank
$\dim_{\mathbb F_p} H^2(G, \mathbb F_p)$ is one. The coefficients
$\mathbb F_p$ have the trivial action. Cohomology is continuous cohomology.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.27»

open CategoryTheory

/-- A profinite group is pro-$p$ if each quotient by an open normal subgroup
is a finite $p$-group. -/
def IsProP (p : ℕ) (G : ProfiniteGrp) : Prop :=
  ∀ U : OpenNormalSubgroup G, IsPGroup p (G ⧸ U.toSubgroup)

/-- A topological group is topologically finitely generated if some finite set
generates a dense subgroup. -/
def IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated (G : ProfiniteGrp) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Finset G, (Subgroup.closure (S : Set G)).topologicalClosure = ⊤

/-- The relation rank of a finitely generated pro-$p$ group is one if
$H^2(G, \mathbb F_p)$, with trivial coefficients, has dimension one. -/
def HasRelationRankOne (p : ℕ) (G : ProfiniteGrp) : Prop :=
  Module.finrank (ZMod p)
    ((continuousCohomology (ZMod p) G 2).obj
      (Action.trivial G (TopModuleCat.of (ZMod p) (ZMod p)))) = 1

/-- An additive group is $p$-primary if every element is annihilated by a
power of $p$. -/
def IsPPrimary (p : ℕ) (A : Type*) [AddCommGroup A] : Prop :=
  ∀ a : A, ∃ k : ℕ, (p ^ k) • a = 0

/-- The $p$-cohomological dimension of a profinite group is at most $d$ if
continuous cohomology vanishes above degree $d$ for every discrete continuous
$p$-primary module. -/
def PCohomologicalDimensionAtMost (p d : ℕ) (G : ProfiniteGrp) : Prop :=
  ∀ (A : Action (TopModuleCat.{0} ℤ) G), DiscreteTopology A.V → A.IsContinuous →
    IsPPrimary p A.V → ∀ n : ℕ, d < n →
      Subsingleton ((continuousCohomology ℤ G n).obj A)

/-- The $p$-cohomological dimension is exactly two. -/
def HasPCohomologicalDimensionTwo (p : ℕ) (G : ProfiniteGrp) : Prop :=
  PCohomologicalDimensionAtMost p 2 G ∧
    ¬ PCohomologicalDimensionAtMost p 1 G

/--
If $p$ is prime and $G$ is a torsion-free pro-$p$ group with a single defining
relation, then $\operatorname{cd}_p G = 2$.

A single defining relation is expressed by finite topological generation and
relation rank $\dim_{\mathbb F_p} H^2(G, \mathbb F_p)=1$; this excludes the
degenerate free case.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.27» :
    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ (G : ProfiniteGrp),
      IsProP p G → IsMulTorsionFree G →
      IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated G → HasRelationRankOne p G →
      HasPCohomologicalDimensionTwo p G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.27»
modeling_decisions: A pro-p group is modeled as a `ProfiniteGrp` whose quotients by all open normal subgroups are `p`-groups.

The standard one-relator convention from the decomposition is modeled by finite topological generation together with `dim_{F_p} H^2(G, F_p) = 1`, using the trivial discrete coefficient module and Mathlib's continuous cohomology.

The p-cohomological dimension is defined through vanishing of continuous cohomology for all discrete, jointly continuous, p-primary integer-linear G-modules. Exact dimension two means dimension at most two but not at most one.
Torsion-freeness uses Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree`, which for groups is equivalent to every nonidentity element having infinite order.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.27

by H. Koch

Prove that if $G$ is a torsion-free pro-$p$-group with a single defining relation, then
$\mathrm{cd}\, G = 2$. This has been proved for a large class of groups in
(J. P. Labute, *Inv. Math.*, **4**, no. 2 (1967), 142–158).

Conventions (Serre, Koch, Labute):
* A pro-$p$ group with a single defining relation is a pro-$p$ group $G \cong F/(r)$, where
  $F$ is a free pro-$p$ group of finite rank, $r \neq 1$ is an element of the Frattini subgroup
  $\Phi(F) = \overline{F^p [F, F]}$ and $(r)$ is the closed normal subgroup of $F$ generated by
  $r$. Equivalently, $G$ is finitely generated with relation rank
  $\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p} H^2(G, \mathbb{Z}/p) = 1$. The condition $r \in \Phi(F)$ excludes the
  degenerate case in which $G$ is itself free pro-$p$ (so $\mathrm{cd}\, G \le 1$ and the
  statement would fail).
* $\mathrm{cd}\, G$ is the cohomological dimension of the profinite group $G$: the least $n$
  such that the continuous cohomology $H^m(G, A)$ vanishes for all $m > n$ and all discrete
  torsion $G$-modules $A$ (Serre, *Cohomologie Galoisienne*, I.3.1). For a pro-$p$ group it
  agrees with the $p$-cohomological dimension $\mathrm{cd}_p\, G$.

*References:*
* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
* J. P. Labute, *Algèbres de Lie et pro-p-groupes définis par une seule relation*,
  Invent. Math. **4** (1967), 142–158.
* J.-P. Serre, *Cohomologie Galoisienne*, Lecture Notes in Math. 5, Chapter I, §3–§4.
-/

open CategoryTheory

universe u

namespace Kourovka.«5.27»

section ContinuousCohomology

variable (G : Type u) [Group G]
variable (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [TopologicalSpace A] [DiscreteTopology A]
  [DistribMulAction G A]

/--
A discrete `G`-module `A` (an abelian group with the discrete topology on which `G` acts by
automorphisms) viewed as an object of `Action (TopModuleCat ℤ) G`, the input of Mathlib's
`continuousCohomology`. Each endomorphism `a ↦ g • a` is continuous because `A` is discrete.
-/
def discreteModuleAction : Action (TopModuleCat ℤ) G where
  V := .of ℤ A
  ρ := MonoidHom.comp
    { toFun f := TopModuleCat.ofHom ⟨f, continuous_of_discreteTopology⟩
      map_one' := rfl
      map_mul' _ _ := rfl }
    (Representation.ofDistribMulAction ℤ G A)

/-- The action of `g : G` on `discreteModuleAction G A` is the given action `a ↦ g • a`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem discreteModuleAction_ρ_apply (g : G) (a : A) :
    ((discreteModuleAction G A).ρ g).hom a = g • a :=
  rfl

variable [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G]

/--
The `n`-th continuous cohomology group $H^n(G, A)$ of the topological group `G` with
coefficients in the discrete `G`-module `A`, i.e. Mathlib's `continuousCohomology` (defined via
continuous homogeneous cochains) applied to `A`. For a profinite group `G` and a discrete
`G`-module `A` with continuous action this is the usual cohomology of profinite groups
(Serre, *Cohomologie Galoisienne*, I.2).
-/
noncomputable def continuousCohomologyGroup (n : ℕ) : Type u :=
  (continuousCohomology ℤ G n).obj (discreteModuleAction G A)

/--
The cohomological dimension $\mathrm{cd}\, G$ of a topological group `G`: the least
$n \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ such that $H^m(G, A) = 0$ for all $m > n$ and all discrete
torsion `G`-modules `A` (Serre, *Cohomologie Galoisienne*, I.3.1); it is `⊤` if there is no such
finite `n`. A discrete `G`-module is an abelian group with the discrete topology together with a
continuous action of `G` by automorphisms.
-/
noncomputable def cohomologicalDimension : ℕ∞ :=
  sInf {n : ℕ∞ | ∀ m : ℕ, n < m →
    ∀ (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [TopologicalSpace A] [DiscreteTopology A]
      [DistribMulAction G A] [ContinuousSMul G A],
      AddMonoid.IsTorsion A → Subsingleton (continuousCohomologyGroup G A m)}

end ContinuousCohomology

/--
A profinite group `G` is a pro-`p` group if all of its continuous finite quotients are
`p`-groups, i.e. every open normal subgroup of `G` has index a power of `p`.
-/
def IsProP (p : ℕ) (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal → IsOpen (N : Set G) → ∃ k : ℕ, N.index = p ^ k

/-- The trivial group is a pro-`p` group for every `p`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isProP_trivial (p : ℕ) : IsProP p (ProfiniteGrp.of PUnit) := by
  intro N _ _
  exact ⟨0, by simp [Subsingleton.elim N ⊤]⟩

/--
A profinite group `F` is a free pro-`p` group on the finite family `x : Fin n → F` (a free
pro-`p` group of rank `n`) if `F` is pro-`p` and every map from the generators `x` to a pro-`p`
group `H` extends uniquely to a continuous homomorphism `F → H`.
-/
def IsFreeProPOn (p : ℕ) {F : ProfiniteGrp.{u}} {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → F) : Prop :=
  IsProP p F ∧ ∀ H : ProfiniteGrp.{u}, IsProP p H →
    ∀ f : Fin n → H, ∃! φ : F ⟶ H, ∀ i, φ (x i) = f i

/--
The Frattini subgroup $\Phi(F) = \overline{F^p [F, F]}$ of a pro-`p` group `F`: the closed
subgroup generated by the `p`-th powers and the commutators of `F`. It is the intersection of
the maximal open subgroups of `F`, and `F / Φ(F)` is the largest elementary abelian quotient
of `F`.
-/
def proPFrattini (p : ℕ) (F : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Subgroup F :=
  (Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun x : F => x ^ p) ⊔ commutator F).topologicalClosure

/--
A profinite group `G` is a pro-`p` group with a single defining relation if $G \cong F/(r)$,
where `F` is a free pro-`p` group of finite rank, `r ≠ 1` is an element of the Frattini subgroup
$\Phi(F)$ and $(r)$ is the closed normal subgroup of `F` generated by `r`. The isomorphism
$G \cong F/(r)$ is expressed by a continuous surjective homomorphism `φ : F → G` with kernel
$(r)$ (a continuous surjection between profinite groups is open, so it induces a topological
isomorphism $F / \ker φ \cong G$).

The condition `r ∈ Φ(F)` says that the presentation is minimal; together with `r ≠ 1` it is
equivalent to the relation rank $\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p} H^2(G, \mathbb{Z}/p)$ of `G` being `1`.
Without it `G` would be a free pro-`p` group of rank `n - 1`.
-/
def HasSingleDefiningRelation (p : ℕ) (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∃ (F : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → F) (r : F) (φ : F ⟶ G),
    IsFreeProPOn p x ∧ r ≠ 1 ∧ r ∈ proPFrattini p F ∧ Function.Surjective φ ∧
      (φ.hom : F →* G).ker = (Subgroup.normalClosure {r}).topologicalClosure

/--
Prove that if $G$ is a torsion-free pro-$p$-group with a single defining relation, then
$\mathrm{cd}\, G = 2$.

Here $G \cong F/(r)$ with $F$ a free pro-$p$ group of finite rank and $1 \neq r \in \Phi(F)$,
torsion-free means that `G` has no nontrivial element of finite order, and $\mathrm{cd}\, G$ is
the cohomological dimension of the profinite group $G$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.27» :
    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) [IsMulTorsionFree G],
      IsProP p G → HasSingleDefiningRelation p G → cohomologicalDimension G = 2 := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.27»

The isomorphism G ≅ F/(r) is expressed as a continuous surjective hom F ⟶ G with kernel the closed normal subgroup generated by r (continuous surjections of profinite groups are open).

Free pro-p group of rank n is defined by the universal property against all pro-p groups H in the same universe u (`∃! φ : F ⟶ H` in `ProfiniteGrp`). The Frattini subgroup is defined concretely as closure(F^p[F,F]) rather than via Mathlib's abstract `frattini`, since the latter uses abstract (not open) maximal subgroups.

Torsion-free is Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree G` (no nontrivial element of finite order); for pro-p groups this is the same as having no element of order p.
The statement is universe-polymorphic in `ProfiniteGrp.{u}`; mathematically the truth value does not depend on u.

/-- A profinite group is pro-$p$ if all its finite continuous quotients are $p$-groups. -/
def IsProP (p : ℕ) (G : ProfiniteGrp.{0}) : Prop :=
  ∀ (Q : Type) [Group Q] [Finite Q] [TopologicalSpace Q] [DiscreteTopology Q]
    (f : G →ₜ* Q), Function.Surjective f → IsPGroup p Q

/-- A topological group is topologically finitely generated if some finite set generates a dense
subgroup. -/
def IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated (G : ProfiniteGrp.{0}) : Prop :=
  ∃ s : Finset G, (Subgroup.closure (s : Set G)).topologicalClosure = ⊤

def trivialFpModule (p : ℕ) (G : ProfiniteGrp.{0}) :
    Action (TopModuleCat (ZMod p)) G :=
  Action.trivial G (TopModuleCat.of (ZMod p) (ZMod p))

/-- A finitely generated pro-$p$ group has relation rank one if
$\dim_{\mathbb F_p} H^2(G, \mathbb F_p)=1$. -/
def HasRelationRankOne (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (G : ProfiniteGrp.{0}) : Prop :=
  Module.rank (ZMod p)
    ((continuousCohomology (ZMod p) G 2).obj (trivialFpModule p G)) = 1

discrete and every element is annihilated by a power of $p$. -/

    (M : Action (TopModuleCat.{0} ℤ) G) : Prop :=
  M.IsContinuous ∧ DiscreteTopology M.V ∧ ∀ x : M.V, ∃ k : ℕ, p ^ k • x = 0

/-- A pro-$p$ group has $p$-cohomological dimension two if
$H^2(G, \mathbb F_p) \ne 0$ and $H^n(G,M)=0$ for every discrete $p$-primary torsion
$G$-module $M$ and every $n>2$. -/

  ¬ Limits.IsZero ((continuousCohomology (ZMod p) G 2).obj (trivialFpModule p G)) ∧
    ∀ (M : Action (TopModuleCat.{0} ℤ) G), IsDiscretePPrimaryModule p G M →
      ∀ n : ℕ, 2 < n → Limits.IsZero ((continuousCohomology ℤ G n).obj M)

$\operatorname{cd}_p G=2$.

/-!
# Conjecture 5.27

by H. Koch

Prove that if $G$ is a torsion-free pro-$p$-group with a single defining relation, then
$\operatorname{cd} G = 2$. This has been proved for a large class of groups in
(J. P. Labute, *Inv. Math.*, **4**, no. 2 (1967), 142--158).

Here a pro-$p$ group with a single defining relation is a pro-$p$ group
$G \cong F / \overline{\langle r \rangle^F}$, where $F$ is a free pro-$p$ group of finite rank
and $1 \ne r \in \Phi(F) = \overline{F^p [F, F]}$ (Serre, *Cohomologie galoisienne*, I.4.3;
Koch, *Galoissche Theorie der p-Erweiterungen*). The condition $r \in \Phi(F)$ says that the
presentation is minimal, i.e. that $\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p} H^2(G, \mathbb{Z}/p) = 1$; without it
$G$ would be a free pro-$p$ group and the claim would fail. Torsion-free means that $G$ has no
non-trivial element of finite order, and $\operatorname{cd} G$ is the cohomological dimension
of the profinite group $G$, defined through continuous cohomology with coefficients in discrete
torsion $G$-modules (Serre, *Cohomologie galoisienne*, I.3.1).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.27»

universe u

/-- A topological group `G` is a pro-`p` group if it is profinite (compact, Hausdorff and
totally disconnected) and every open normal subgroup has index a power of `p`. -/
structure IsProPGroup (p : ℕ) (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] : Prop where
  compactSpace : CompactSpace G
  t2Space : T2Space G
  totallyDisconnectedSpace : TotallyDisconnectedSpace G
  exists_index_eq_pow : ∀ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal → IsOpen (N : Set G) →
    ∃ k : ℕ, N.index = p ^ k

/-- `F` is a free pro-`p` group on the basis `x : Fin n → F`: `F` is a pro-`p` group and every
map `f : Fin n → H` into a pro-`p` group `H` extends uniquely to a continuous homomorphism
`F →ₜ* H` with `x i ↦ f i`. -/
def IsFreeProPGroupOn (p : ℕ) {F : Type u} [Group F] [TopologicalSpace F]
    [IsTopologicalGroup F] {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → F) : Prop :=
  IsProPGroup p F ∧
    ∀ (H : Type u) [Group H] [TopologicalSpace H] [IsTopologicalGroup H], IsProPGroup p H →
      ∀ f : Fin n → H, ∃! φ : F →ₜ* H, ∀ i, φ (x i) = f i

/-- The Frattini subgroup $\Phi(F) = \overline{F^p [F, F]}$ of a pro-`p` group `F`: the closure
of the subgroup generated by the `p`-th powers and the commutators. -/
def frattiniProP (p : ℕ) (F : Type u) [Group F] [TopologicalSpace F] [IsTopologicalGroup F] :
    Subgroup F :=
  (Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun y : F => y ^ p) ⊔ commutator F).topologicalClosure

/-- A topological group `G` is a pro-`p` group with a single defining relation if
$G \cong F / N$ as topological groups, where `F` is a free pro-`p` group of finite rank,
$N = \overline{\langle r \rangle^F}$ is the closed normal subgroup of `F` generated by an element
`r` with $1 \ne r \in \Phi(F) = \overline{F^p [F, F]}$.

The condition $r \in \Phi(F)$ says that the presentation is minimal, so that
$\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p} H^2(G, \mathbb{Z}/p) = 1$; without it `G` would be a free pro-`p` group. -/
def HasSingleDefiningRelation (p : ℕ) (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (F : Type u) (_ : Group F) (_ : TopologicalSpace F) (_ : IsTopologicalGroup F)
    (x : Fin n → F) (r : F) (N : Subgroup F) (_ : N.Normal),
    IsFreeProPGroupOn p x ∧ r ≠ 1 ∧ r ∈ frattiniProP p F ∧
      N = (Subgroup.normalClosure {r}).topologicalClosure ∧ Nonempty (F ⧸ N ≃ₜ* G)

section Cohomology

variable {G : Type} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]

/-- A `G`-module `A` (a `ℤ`-linear representation of `G`) is a discrete torsion `G`-module if
every element of `A` has finite order and the action of `G` is continuous for the discrete
topology on `A`, i.e. every stabiliser $\{g \in G \mid g a = a\}$ is open. -/
def IsDiscreteTorsionModule (A : Rep ℤ G) : Prop :=
  (∀ a : A, IsOfFinAddOrder a) ∧ ∀ a : A, IsOpen {g : G | A.ρ g a = a}

/-- The continuous cohomology group $H^n(G, A)$ of the topological group `G` with coefficients
in the discrete `G`-module `A` vanishes. It is computed by the complex of continuous (i.e.
locally constant, since `A` is discrete) inhomogeneous cochains
$C^n(G, A) = \{f \colon G^n \to A \text{ locally constant}\}$, with the standard differential
`inhomogeneousCochains.d`. So $H^0(G, A) = 0$ means that every $0$-cocycle is zero, and for
$n \ge 1$, $H^n(G, A) = 0$ means that every locally constant $n$-cocycle is the coboundary of a
locally constant $(n-1)$-cochain. -/
def IsZeroContinuousCohomology (A : Rep ℤ G) : ℕ → Prop
  | 0 => ∀ f : (Fin 0 → G) → A, inhomogeneousCochains.d A 0 f = 0 → f = 0
  | n + 1 => ∀ f : (Fin (n + 1) → G) → A, IsLocallyConstant f →
      inhomogeneousCochains.d A (n + 1) f = 0 →
        ∃ g : (Fin n → G) → A, IsLocallyConstant g ∧ inhomogeneousCochains.d A n g = f

variable (G) in
/-- The cohomological dimension $\operatorname{cd} G$ of the topological group `G`: the
smallest $n \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ such that $H^m(G, A) = 0$ for all $m > n$ and all
discrete torsion `G`-modules `A`. -/
noncomputable def cohomologicalDimension : ℕ∞ :=
  sInf {n : ℕ∞ | ∀ A : Rep ℤ G, IsDiscreteTorsionModule A →
    ∀ m : ℕ, n < m → IsZeroContinuousCohomology A m}

end Cohomology

Prove that if $G$ is a torsion-free pro-$p$-group with a single defining relation, then
$\operatorname{cd} G = 2$.

Here $G$ has a single defining relation if $G \cong F / \overline{\langle r \rangle^F}$ with $F$
a free pro-$p$ group of finite rank and $1 \ne r \in \Phi(F) = \overline{F^p [F, F]}$;
torsion-free means that $G$ has no non-trivial element of finite order; and
$\operatorname{cd} G$ is the cohomological dimension of the profinite group $G$.
-/

    [IsTopologicalGroup G] (hG : IsProPGroup p G) (htf : ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ¬ IsOfFinOrder g)
    (hrel : HasSingleDefiningRelation p G) :
    cohomologicalDimension G = 2 := by
  sorry

/-- The trivial group is a pro-`p` group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isProPGroup_punit (p : ℕ) : IsProPGroup p PUnit where
  compactSpace := inferInstance
  t2Space := inferInstance
  totallyDisconnectedSpace := inferInstance
  exists_index_eq_pow N _ _ := ⟨0, by simp [Subsingleton.elim N ⊤]⟩

/-- The cyclic group of order `p` is a pro-`p` group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isProPGroup_multiplicative_zmod (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] :
    IsProPGroup p (Multiplicative (ZMod p)) where
  compactSpace := inferInstance
  t2Space := inferInstance
  totallyDisconnectedSpace := inferInstance
  exists_index_eq_pow N _ _ := by
    have h : N.index ∣ p := by
      simpa [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, ZMod.card] using N.index_dvd_card
    rcases (Fact.out : p.Prime).eq_one_or_self_of_dvd _ h with h | h
    · exact ⟨0, by simp [h]⟩
    · exact ⟨1, by simp [h]⟩

/-- The trivial group is the free pro-`p` group of rank `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFreeProPGroupOn_punit (p : ℕ) : IsFreeProPGroupOn p (Fin.elim0 : Fin 0 → PUnit) := by
  refine ⟨isProPGroup_punit p, fun H _ _ _ _ f => ⟨1, fun i => i.elim0, fun φ _ => ?_⟩⟩
  ext x
  simpa using map_one φ

/-- `ℤ/p` with the trivial action is a discrete torsion `G`-module. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isDiscreteTorsionModule_trivial_zmod {G : Type} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] (p : ℕ)
    [NeZero p] : IsDiscreteTorsionModule (Rep.trivial ℤ G (ZMod p)) :=
  ⟨fun a => isOfFinAddOrder_of_finite a, fun a => by simp⟩

end Kourovka.«5.27»

modeling_decisions: Pro-p group is defined as: profinite (CompactSpace, T2Space, TotallyDisconnectedSpace topological group) with every open normal subgroup of p-power index (`Subgroup.index = p ^ k`). This is the standard equivalent of 'inverse limit of finite p-groups'. T2Space is redundant given total disconnectedness but included for literalness.

'G ≅ F/⟨⟨r⟩⟩' is formalized as `Nonempty (F ⧸ N ≃ₜ* G)` with N a normal subgroup equal to `(Subgroup.normalClosure {r}).topologicalClosure`, i.e. an isomorphism of topological groups with the quotient topology on F ⧸ N. Both `r ≠ 1` and `r ∈ Φ(F)` are required, as prescribed by the decomposition notes (excludes the degenerate free case).

The hypothesis `IsProPGroup p G` in the theorem is mathematically implied by `HasSingleDefiningRelation p G` (a quotient of a pro-p group by a closed normal subgroup is pro-p) but is kept because the statement says 'G is a torsion-free pro-p group'.

Torsion-free is stated as `∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ¬ IsOfFinOrder g`. Mathlib's class `IsMulTorsionFree` was deliberately NOT used: it asserts injectivity of x ↦ x^n for n ≠ 0, which is strictly stronger than 'no nontrivial element of finite order' for non-abelian groups (`isMulTorsionFree_iff_not_isOfFinOrder` needs `CommGroup`).

Prove that if $G$ is a torsion-free pro-$p$-group with a single defining relation, then
$\mathrm{cd}\, G = 2$. This has been proved for a large class of groups in
(J. P. Labute, *Inv. Math.*, **4**, no. 2 (1967), 142–158).

Mathlib does not yet have the cohomology of profinite groups. This file therefore defines the
cohomology of a topological group $G$ with coefficients in a discrete $G$-module $A$ as the
cohomology of the complex of continuous (i.e. locally constant) inhomogeneous cochains
$G^n \to A$ (Serre, *Galois Cohomology*, Chapter I, §2), and defines the cohomological dimension
$\mathrm{cd}\, G$ from it (Serre, Chapter I, §3). The differential is the one used by Mathlib for
the cohomology of abstract groups (`inhomogeneousCochains.d`); see `cochainD_eq`.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
- J. P. Labute, *Algèbres de Lie et pro-p-groupes définis par une seule relation*,
  Invent. Math. **4** (1967), 142–158.
- J.-P. Serre, *Galois Cohomology*, Springer, Chapter I.
-/

universe u

section ContinuousCohomology

variable {k G A : Type*} [CommRing k] [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [AddCommGroup A] [Module k A]
  (ρ : Representation k G A)

/-- A $G$-module $A$ (given as a $k$-linear representation `ρ` of `G` on `A`) is *discrete* if
the action $G \times A \to A$ is continuous for the discrete topology on $A$, i.e. every orbit
map $g \mapsto g \cdot a$ is locally constant (equivalently, all stabilizers are open). -/
def IsDiscreteModule : Prop :=
  ∀ a : A, IsLocallyConstant fun g : G ↦ ρ g a

/-- The differential of inhomogeneous cochains. It sends $f \colon G^n \to A$ to the function
$(g_0, \dots, g_n) \mapsto \rho(g_0)(f(g_1, \dots, g_n))
+ \sum_{i = 0}^{n - 1} (-1)^{i + 1} f(g_0, \dots, g_i g_{i + 1}, \dots, g_n)
+ (-1)^{n + 1} f(g_0, \dots, g_{n - 1})$. -/
def cochainD (n : ℕ) : ((Fin n → G) → A) →ₗ[k] ((Fin (n + 1) → G) → A) where
  toFun f g :=
    ρ (g 0) (f fun i ↦ g i.succ) + ∑ j : Fin (n + 1),
      (-1 : k) ^ ((j : ℕ) + 1) • f (Fin.contractNth j (· * ·) g)
  map_add' f g := by
    ext
    simp [Finset.sum_add_distrib, add_add_add_comm]
  map_smul' r f := by
    ext
    simp [Finset.smul_sum, ← smul_assoc, mul_comm r]

variable (k G A) in
/-- The continuous `n`-cochains: the locally constant functions $G^n \to A$, i.e. the maps that
are continuous for the discrete topology on $A$. -/
def contCochains (n : ℕ) : Submodule k ((Fin n → G) → A) where
  carrier := {f | IsLocallyConstant f}
  zero_mem' := IsLocallyConstant.zero
  add_mem' hf hg := hf.add hg
  smul_mem' c _ hf := hf.comp (c • ·)

/-- The continuous `n`-cocycles: the continuous `n`-cochains killed by the differential. -/
def contCocycles (n : ℕ) : Submodule k ((Fin n → G) → A) :=
  contCochains k G A n ⊓ LinearMap.ker (cochainD ρ n)

/-- The continuous `n`-coboundaries: the images of the continuous `(n - 1)`-cochains under the
differential (there are no coboundaries in degree `0`). -/
def contCoboundaries : (n : ℕ) → Submodule k ((Fin n → G) → A)
  | 0 => ⊥
  | n + 1 => (contCochains k G A n).map (cochainD ρ n)

/-- The `n`-th continuous cohomology group $H^n(G, A)$ of the topological group $G$ with
coefficients in the $G$-module $A$: continuous cocycles modulo continuous coboundaries. -/
abbrev contCohomology (n : ℕ) : Type _ :=
  contCocycles ρ n ⧸ (contCoboundaries ρ n).comap (contCocycles ρ n).subtype

/-- The trivial module is a discrete module. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isDiscreteModule_trivial : IsDiscreteModule (Representation.trivial k G A) :=
  fun a ↦ by simpa using IsLocallyConstant.const (X := G) a

/-- For a discrete module, the differential maps continuous cochains to continuous cochains. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem cochainD_mem_contCochains [ContinuousMul G] (hρ : IsDiscreteModule ρ) {n : ℕ}
    {f : (Fin n → G) → A} (hf : f ∈ contCochains k G A n) :
    cochainD ρ n f ∈ contCochains k G A (n + 1) := by
  change IsLocallyConstant fun g ↦ ρ (g 0) (f fun i ↦ g i.succ) + ∑ j : Fin (n + 1),
      (-1 : k) ^ ((j : ℕ) + 1) • f (Fin.contractNth j (· * ·) g)
  refine IsLocallyConstant.add ?_ ?_
  · rw [IsLocallyConstant.iff_eventually_eq]
    intro g
    have h1 := ((hf : IsLocallyConstant f).comp_continuous
      (f := fun g' : Fin (n + 1) → G ↦ fun i ↦ g' i.succ) (by fun_prop)).eventually_eq g
    have h2 := ((hρ (f fun i ↦ g i.succ)).comp_continuous
      (continuous_apply (0 : Fin (n + 1)))).eventually_eq g
    filter_upwards [h1, h2] with g' h1 h2
    simp only [Function.comp] at h1 h2
    rw [h1, h2]
  · have : (fun g : Fin (n + 1) → G ↦ ∑ j : Fin (n + 1),
        (-1 : k) ^ ((j : ℕ) + 1) • f (Fin.contractNth j (· * ·) g)) =
        ∑ j : Fin (n + 1), fun g ↦
          (-1 : k) ^ ((j : ℕ) + 1) • f (Fin.contractNth j (· * ·) g) := by
      ext g; simp
    rw [this]
    refine Finset.sum_induction _ _ (fun _ _ ha hb ↦ ha.add hb) IsLocallyConstant.zero
      fun j _ ↦ ?_
    have hc : Continuous fun g : Fin (n + 1) → G ↦ Fin.contractNth j (· * ·) g :=
      continuous_pi fun i ↦ by
        unfold Fin.contractNth
        split_ifs
        · exact continuous_apply _
        · exact (continuous_apply _).mul (continuous_apply _)
        · exact continuous_apply _
    exact ((hf : IsLocallyConstant f).comp_continuous hc).comp _

end ContinuousCohomology

section Comparison

variable {k G A : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G] [AddCommGroup A] [Module k A]

/-- The differential `cochainD` is the differential of the inhomogeneous cochain complex used by
Mathlib to define the cohomology of abstract groups. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem cochainD_eq (B : Rep k G) (n : ℕ) :
    cochainD B.ρ n = (inhomogeneousCochains.d B n).hom := by
  ext f g
  simp [cochainD, inhomogeneousCochains.d_hom_apply]

/-- The differential squares to zero. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem cochainD_cochainD (ρ : Representation k G A) (n : ℕ) (f : (Fin n → G) → A) :
    cochainD ρ (n + 1) (cochainD ρ n f) = 0 := by
  have := LinearMap.congr_fun (congrArg ModuleCat.Hom.hom
    (groupCohomology.inhomogeneousCochains.d_comp_d n (Rep.of ρ))) f
  simpa [cochainD_eq] using this

/-- For a discrete module, continuous coboundaries are continuous cocycles, so that
`contCohomology` is the quotient of the continuous cocycles by the continuous coboundaries. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem contCoboundaries_le_contCocycles [TopologicalSpace G] [ContinuousMul G]
    (ρ : Representation k G A) (hρ : IsDiscreteModule ρ) (n : ℕ) :
    contCoboundaries ρ n ≤ contCocycles ρ n := by
  cases n with
  | zero => exact bot_le
  | succ n =>
    rintro _ ⟨f, hf, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨cochainD_mem_contCochains ρ hρ hf, cochainD_cochainD ρ n f⟩

end Comparison

/-- The cohomological dimension $\mathrm{cd}\, G$ of a topological group $G$: the supremum of the
$n$ such that $H^n(G, A) \neq 0$ for some discrete torsion $G$-module $A$
(Serre, *Galois Cohomology*, I.3.1). -/
noncomputable def cohomologicalDimension (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨆ (n : ℕ) (_ : ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup A) (ρ : Representation ℤ G A),
    IsDiscreteModule ρ ∧ AddMonoid.IsTorsion A ∧ Nontrivial (contCohomology ρ n)),
      (n : ℕ∞)

/-- A profinite group `G` is a pro-`p` group if all of its quotients by open normal subgroups are

def IsProPGroup (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] : Prop :=
  ∀ N : OpenNormalSubgroup G, IsPGroup p (G ⧸ (N : Subgroup G))

/-- A $p$-group is a pro-`p` group for any group topology. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isProPGroup_of_isPGroup {p : ℕ} {G : Type*} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
    (h : IsPGroup p G) : IsProPGroup p G :=
  fun N ↦ h.to_quotient (N : Subgroup G)

/--
Prove that if $G$ is a torsion-free pro-$p$-group with a single defining relation, then
$\mathrm{cd}\, G = 2$.

/-- A profinite group is pro-$p$ if all its finite quotients by open normal
subgroups are $p$-groups. -/
def IsProP (p : ℕ) (G : ProfiniteGrp) : Prop :=
  ∀ N : OpenNormalSubgroup G, IsPGroup p (G ⧸ N.toSubgroup)

/-- A profinite group is topologically finitely generated if some finite set
generates a dense abstract subgroup. -/
def IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated (G : ProfiniteGrp) : Prop :=
  ∃ s : Finset G, Dense (Subgroup.closure (s : Set G) : Set G)

/-- A finitely generated pro-$p$ group has one defining relation when its
relation rank, $\dim_{\mathbb F_p} H^2(G,\mathbb F_p)$, is one. -/
def HasOneDefiningRelation (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (G : ProfiniteGrp) : Prop :=
  IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated G ∧
    Module.finrank (ZMod p)
      ((continuousCohomology (ZMod p) G 2).obj
        (Action.trivial G (TopModuleCat.of (ZMod p) (ZMod p)))) = 1

/-- The $p$-cohomological dimension of a profinite group is exactly $d$ if
continuous cohomology with coefficients in every discrete continuous
$p$-primary module vanishes above $d$, and is nonzero in degree $d$ for some
such module. -/
def HasPCohomologicalDimension (p d : ℕ) (G : ProfiniteGrp) : Prop :=
  (∀ (M : Action (TopModuleCat.{0} ℤ) G), M.IsContinuous → DiscreteTopology M.V →
      (∀ x : M.V, ∃ n : ℕ, (p : ℤ) ^ n • x = 0) →
      ∀ q : ℕ, d < q → IsZero ((continuousCohomology ℤ G q).obj M)) ∧
    ∃ M : Action (TopModuleCat.{0} ℤ) G, M.IsContinuous ∧ DiscreteTopology M.V ∧
      (∀ x : M.V, ∃ n : ℕ, (p : ℤ) ^ n • x = 0) ∧
      ¬ IsZero ((continuousCohomology ℤ G d).obj M)

If $G$ is a torsion-free pro-$p$ group with a single defining relation, then
$\operatorname{cd}_p G=2$.
-/

    ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (G : ProfiniteGrp),
      IsProP p G → IsMulTorsionFree G → HasOneDefiningRelation p G →
      HasPCohomologicalDimension p 2 G := by

# Conjecture 5.27

by H. Koch

$\operatorname{cd} G = 2$. This has been proved for a large class of groups in
(J. P. Labute, *Inv. Math.*, **4**, no. 2 (1967), 142–158).

Following the standard convention (Serre, Koch, Labute), a pro-$p$ group *with a single
defining relation* is a group of the form $G \cong F/(r)$, where $F$ is a free pro-$p$ group of
finite rank, $(r)$ is the closed normal subgroup generated by a single element $r \neq 1$, and
$r$ lies in the Frattini subgroup $\Phi(F) = \overline{F^p[F, F]}$, so that the presentation is
minimal (equivalently, $\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p} H^2(G, \mathbb{Z}/p) = 1$). Without the condition
$r \in \Phi(F)$ the quotient $F/(r)$ would be a free pro-$p$ group of smaller rank, for which
$\operatorname{cd} \leq 1$.

Here $\operatorname{cd} G$ is the cohomological dimension of the profinite group $G$: the
supremum of the $n$ such that $H^n(G, A) \neq 0$ for some discrete torsion $G$-module $A$,
where $H^n$ denotes continuous cohomology. For a pro-$p$ group this coincides with the
$p$-cohomological dimension $\operatorname{cd}_p G$.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 5.27.

namespace Kourovka.«5.27»

open CategoryTheory

universe u

/-- A profinite group $G$ is a pro-$p$ group if every finite continuous quotient $G/U$, for
$U$ an open normal subgroup of $G$, is a $p$-group. Equivalently, $G$ is an inverse limit of
finite $p$-groups. -/
def IsProP (p : ℕ) (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ U : OpenNormalSubgroup G, IsPGroup p (G ⧸ U.toSubgroup)

/-- The trivial group is a pro-$p$ group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isProP_unit (p : ℕ) : IsProP p (ProfiniteGrp.of Unit) := fun _ g =>
  ⟨0, by
    rw [pow_zero, pow_one]
    obtain ⟨⟨⟩, rfl⟩ := QuotientGroup.mk_surjective g
    rfl⟩

/-- The family $x = (x_1, \dots, x_n)$ is a free basis of the pro-$p$ group $F$, i.e. $F$ is
the free pro-$p$ group of rank $n$ on $x_1, \dots, x_n$: $F$ is a pro-$p$ group, and for every
pro-$p$ group $H$ and every choice of elements $h_1, \dots, h_n \in H$ there is a unique
continuous homomorphism $\varphi \colon F \to H$ with $\varphi(x_i) = h_i$ for all $i$. -/
def IsFreeProPBasis (p : ℕ) {n : ℕ} {F : ProfiniteGrp.{u}} (x : Fin n → F) : Prop :=
  IsProP p F ∧
    ∀ (H : ProfiniteGrp.{u}), IsProP p H → ∀ h : Fin n → H, ∃! φ : F ⟶ H, ∀ i, φ (x i) = h i

/-- The Frattini subgroup $\Phi(F) = \overline{F^p [F, F]}$ of a pro-$p$ group $F$: the closure
of the subgroup generated by all $p$-th powers and all commutators. -/
def proPFrattini (p : ℕ) (F : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Subgroup F :=
  (Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun g : F => g ^ p) ⊔ commutator F).topologicalClosure

/-- The Frattini subgroup $\Phi(F)$ is a normal subgroup of $F$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem proPFrattini_normal (p : ℕ) (F : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : (proPFrattini p F).Normal := by
  have : (Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun g : F => g ^ p)).Normal := by
    suffices h : Set.range (fun g : F => g ^ p) =
        Group.conjugatesOfSet (Set.range fun g : F => g ^ p) by
      rw [h]
      exact Subgroup.normalClosure_normal
    refine Set.Subset.antisymm Group.subset_conjugatesOfSet fun a ha => ?_
    simp_rw [Group.mem_conjugatesOfSet_iff, isConj_iff] at ha
    obtain ⟨b, ⟨c, rfl⟩, d, rfl⟩ := ha
    exact ⟨d * c * d⁻¹, conj_pow⟩
  exact Subgroup.is_normal_topologicalClosure _

/-- A pro-$p$ group $G$ has a single defining relation if $G \cong F/(r)$, where $F$ is a free
pro-$p$ group of finite rank $n$ and $(r)$ is the closed normal subgroup of $F$ generated by a
single element $r \neq 1$ lying in the Frattini subgroup $\Phi(F)$ (so that the presentation is
minimal). The isomorphism $F/(r) \cong G$ is encoded by a continuous surjective homomorphism
$\varphi \colon F \to G$ with kernel $(r)$; since $F$ is compact and $G$ is Hausdorff, such a
$\varphi$ induces an isomorphism of topological groups $F/(r) \cong G$. -/
def HasSingleDefiningRelation (p : ℕ) (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (F : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) (x : Fin n → F) (r : F) (φ : F ⟶ G),
    IsFreeProPBasis p x ∧ r ≠ 1 ∧ r ∈ proPFrattini p F ∧ Function.Surjective φ ∧
      φ.hom.toMonoidHom.ker = (Subgroup.normalClosure {r}).topologicalClosure

/-- A discrete torsion $G$-module for a profinite group $G$: a topological abelian group $A$
carrying the discrete topology, all of whose elements have finite order, together with an
action of $G$ by group automorphisms such that the action map $G \times A \to A$ is continuous
(equivalently, all stabilisers are open). -/
def IsDiscreteTorsionModule (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) (A : Action (TopModuleCat.{u} ℤ) G) : Prop :=
  DiscreteTopology A.V ∧ AddMonoid.IsTorsion A.V ∧
    Continuous fun ga : G × A.V => (A.ρ ga.1).hom ga.2

/-- The cohomological dimension $\operatorname{cd} G \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ of a
profinite group $G$: the supremum of all $n$ for which $H^n(G, A) \neq 0$ for some discrete
torsion $G$-module $A$. Here $H^n(G, A)$ is the continuous cohomology of $G$ with coefficients
in $A$ (computed by continuous homogeneous cochains). -/
noncomputable def cohomologicalDimension (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨆ (n : ℕ) (_ : ∃ A : Action (TopModuleCat.{u} ℤ) G,
    IsDiscreteTorsionModule G A ∧ Nontrivial ((continuousCohomology ℤ G n).obj A)), (n : ℕ∞)

/--
Prove that if $G$ is a torsion-free pro-$p$-group with a single defining relation, then
$\operatorname{cd} G = 2$.

Here $p$ is a prime, "torsion-free" means that $G$ has no non-trivial element of finite order,
"with a single defining relation" means $G \cong F/(r)$ with $F$ free pro-$p$ of finite rank
and $1 \neq r \in \Phi(F)$, and $\operatorname{cd} G$ is the cohomological dimension of the
profinite group $G$. (The hypothesis that $G$ is pro-$p$ is implied by the presentation; it is
kept to mirror the wording of the problem.)
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.27» (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) (hG : IsProP p G)
    (hrel : HasSingleDefiningRelation p G) (htf : ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1) :
    cohomologicalDimension G = 2 := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.27»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The table's single slot and its convention for 'single defining relation' (minimal one-relator presentation, r ∈ Φ(F), excluding the free case) match Serre/Koch/Labute. Side note unrelated to this slot: the repository's Wikipedia/Kaplansky.lean uses `IsMulTorsionFree` for 'torsion-free group', which for non-abelian groups is stronger than the standard notion.
modeling_decisions: 'Torsion-free' is stated literally as `∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1`, NOT as Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree G`: the latter means x ↦ x^n is injective for all n ≠ 0, which for non-abelian groups is strictly stronger (unique roots; e.g. the pro-2 Klein-bottle group ⟨a,b | bab⁻¹a⟩ is a torsion-free one-relator pro-2 group with (ab)² = b², ab ≠ b). Mathlib's equivalence `isMulTorsionFree_iff_not_isOfFinOrder` holds only for `CommGroup`.

'Single defining relation' follows the standard convention given in the decomposition table: G ≅ F/(r) with F free pro-p of finite rank n and 1 ≠ r ∈ Φ(F) = closure(F^p[F,F]); this excludes the degenerate case r ∉ Φ(F) where F/(r) is free of rank n−1. Finite rank is required as in the table (the infinitely generated case reduces to it anyway).
The free pro-p group is characterised by its universal property with respect to pro-p groups H in the same universe as F (`ProfiniteGrp.{u}`); this determines F up to isomorphism.

The isomorphism G ≅ F/(r) is encoded as a continuous surjective homomorphism φ : F ⟶ G (a `ProfiniteGrp` morphism) with kernel equal to `(Subgroup.normalClosure {r}).topologicalClosure`; for compact F and Hausdorff G this is equivalent to a topological group isomorphism F/(r) ≅ G.

Cohomological dimension is the full cd(G) (all discrete torsion modules, Serre I.3.1), not cd_p; for pro-p groups the two agree. Coefficient modules range over `Action (TopModuleCat.{u} ℤ) G` in the same universe as G; mathematically the universe is irrelevant (finite simple modules suffice to detect cd).

Continuous cohomology is Mathlib's `continuousCohomology`, defined via G-invariant homogeneous cochains in the iterated function space C(G, C(G, …, A)). For compact (profinite) G this coincides with the usual continuous cochain cohomology of Serre/Koch; the topology on the cohomology object is ignored (only `Nontrivial` of the carrier is used).
The hypothesis `hG : IsProP p G` is redundant (a quotient of a pro-p group is pro-p) and is kept only to mirror the wording 'G is a torsion-free pro-p group with a single defining relation'.
Since H^2(G, ℤ/p) ≠ 0 forces cd G ≥ 2, the statement `cohomologicalDimension G = 2` is equivalent to cd G ≤ 2, as in the source; the equality is stated verbatim.

The pro-p Frattini subgroup is defined as the topological closure of ⟨p-th powers⟩ ⊔ commutator rather than Mathlib's abstract `frattini` (intersection of maximal subgroups), to avoid relying on the theorem that maximal subgroups of finitely generated pro-p groups are open.
